clusters.name: Broad Blade Convergence
clusters.identity_narrative: A loose medieval warband defined by close-quarters fighters who sweep wide arcs of destruction, drawing equally from physical force, wind, and fire rather than any single elemental discipline. Their identity is forged through battlefield proximity and overlapping damage rather than doctrine or lineage.

clusters.name: Loess Cannon Wardens
clusters.identity_narrative: Rooted in east Asian medieval tradition, these ranged combatants channel earth's mass into wide-arc barrages that reshape terrain and scatter formations across broad killing grounds. Their craft favors patient accumulation over sudden strikes — pressure built from the ground up, released in cascading soil and ember.

clusters.name: Broadfield Convergence Wardens
clusters.identity_narrative: A loose medieval European cohort defined by sweeping ranged volleys that scatter physical, shadow, lightning, fire, and holy force across wide ground — no single element dominates, suggesting practitioners who read the field and adapt rather than specialize. Their identity is forged in the geometry of wide-area suppression rather than any creed or bloodline.

clusters.name: Ironfield Tide Wardens
clusters.identity_narrative: A close-quarters fighting force rooted in European medieval martial tradition, these warriors drive wide sweeping engagements with blunt physical dominance supplemented by water, wind, and holy channeling. Their battlefield presence is defined by broad area suppression at melee range rather than precision or range.

relationships.shared_history_hook: Both factions developed their wide-arc tactical philosophies in response to the same problem: breaking dense enemy formations across broad killing grounds.

Their shared anchor in physical-dominant, multi-element wide-area doctrine suggests a common operational inheritance — two cohorts that drew from the same battlefield philosophy and then developed it in opposing directions.

relationships.tension_narrative: The Broad Blade Convergence and the Ironfield Tide Wardens occupy the same close-quarters, wide-sweep battlefield space, each claiming dominance through physical force and multi-element area suppression. Where the Convergence draws identity from fluid, doctrine-free battlefield improvisation, the Tide Wardens enforce structured medieval-martial discipline — two expressions of the same destructive range that cannot coexist without one subordinating the other.
relationships.shared_history_hook: Both factions evolved around overlapping physical-dominant, close-quarters-AOE combat doctrine, suggesting a shared origin in the same theater of wide-sweep melee engagement before their methods diverged.

The moderate named-anchor overlap between the two factions suggests they have encountered the same theaters of wide-area suppression and drawn competing conclusions about how ranged doctrine should be practiced.

Both factions share an operational vocabulary built around wide-area suppression and formation-breaking, suggesting a common doctrinal inheritance even as their cultural lineages and engagement distances diverged.

relationships.tension_narrative: Both the Broadfield Convergence Wardens and the Ironfield Tide Wardens claim the same European medieval martial ground and share physical dominance as their foundation, yet they have carved opposing doctrines from that shared stock — one projecting multi-element suppression across wide range, the other driving close-quarters AOE through blunt melee presence. The contest between adaptive field control at distance and physical-dominant tide-pushing at close quarters defines a persistent friction over which form of broad-area suppression is the truer expression of their common tradition.
relationships.shared_history_hook: Both factions draw from the same European medieval martial lineage and physical-element core, suggesting a common institutional or regional origin from which their divergent battlefield doctrines emerged.
